source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P103 (late 2nd / early 3rd c. CE; Oxford P.Oxy 4403) preserves Mt 13:55-57 — the Nazareth-rejection / 'is not this the carpenter's son' passage. The P103 readings substantially agree with Vaticanus + Sinaiticus.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + P103 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + P103 readings per Oxyrhynchus Papyri 64 (Comfort & Barrett *Text of the Earliest NT Greek MSS* 2001).
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). P103 = P.Oxy 4403 (late 2nd / early 3rd c. CE; Oxford). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997 (vol 2); Luz Hermeneia 2001-2007 (vol 2); France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Jeremias, J., *The Parables of Jesus* (Scribner's 1972); Snodgrass, K., *Stories with Intent* (Eerdmans 2008); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The P103 cross-collation for vv.55-57 confirms the consensus reading. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·
verses.translit: En tē hēmera ekeinē exelthōn ho Iēsous tēs oikias ekathēto para tēn thalassan·
verses.notes: PARABLE-DISCOURSE OPENING (Discourse 3 of the Matthean five — paralleling Numbers in the pentateuchal-typology). *thalassa* = Sea of Galilee. The seated-by-the-lake setting frames the parable chapter.

verses.text: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.
verses.translit: kai synēchthēsan pros auton ochloi polloi, hōste auton eis ploion embanta kathēsthai, kai pas ho ochlos epi ton aigialon heistēkei.
verses.notes: BOAT-PULPIT SETTING. Sound-amplification by the natural-amphitheater of the Galilean shoreline (the Cove of the Sower near Tabgha) has been experimentally confirmed. France NICNT 503-504.

verses.text: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.
verses.translit: kai elalēsen autois polla en parabolais legōn· Idou exēlthen ho speirōn tou speirein.
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK SITE — THE PARABLE OF THE SOWER OPENING**. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE — THE CANON'S MOST LOAD-BEARING MATTHEW ENGAGEMENT.** Raël *The Role of Christ* reads vv.3-9 + 18-23 (Parable of the Sower) as 'the description of life being seeded on multiple worlds' — the four soil-types are interpreted literally as four planet-types receiving the Elohim panspermia. **HIGHEST LENS-RISK SITE IN THE ENTIRE MATTHEW TRANSLATION.** Acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework MUST be applied at the Editor stage. **PHILOLOGICALLY**: *parabolē* = comparison / similitude / proverb / riddle — translating Hebrew *māšāl*. The standard reading: agricultural-imagery parable about types of hearers/responses to the kingdom-message. *speirōn* = sower. **EDITOR DO NOT PRE-RESOLVE either toward (a) the panspermia reading or (b) the conventional Christian missionary-typology reading**; preserve the agricultural surface-image and document the canon-citation in the apparatus. Davies-Allison ICC 2.376-380; Jeremias 1972; Snodgrass 2008 145-177; Luz Hermeneia 2.235-247.

verses.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.
verses.translit: kai en tō speirein auton ha men epesen para tēn hodon, kai elthonta ta peteina katephagen auta.
verses.notes: FIRST SOIL — path-side. Standard Galilean sowing practice: broadcast-sowing across the field, including the foot-path that bisected unenclosed plots. Seeds falling on the path remain on the surface (compacted earth) and are eaten by birds. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian 'unsuitable planet 1' reading; preserve agricultural surface.

verses.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς.
verses.translit: alla de epesen epi ta petrōdē hopou ouk eichen gēn pollēn, kai eutheōs exaneteilen dia to mē echein bathos gēs.
verses.notes: SECOND SOIL — rocky ground. Galilean limestone bedrock with thin topsoil — common in the area. Quick germination but no root-depth. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian 'unsuitable planet 2'; preserve.

verses.text: ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
verses.translit: hēliou de anateilantos ekaumatisthē kai dia to mē echein rhizan exēranthē.
verses.notes: Scorching-and-withering of the rocky-soil seedling. cf. Jas 1:11 for similar imagery.

verses.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτά.
verses.translit: alla de epesen epi tas akanthas, kai anebēsan hai akanthai kai apepnixan auta.
verses.notes: THIRD SOIL — thorns. *akanthai* — thorny weeds. *apepnixan* (choked off) — competition for water/nutrients. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian 'unsuitable planet 3'; preserve agricultural surface.

verses.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
verses.translit: alla de epesen epi tēn gēn tēn kalēn kai edidou karpon, ho men hekaton ho de hexēkonta ho de triakonta.
verses.notes: FOURTH SOIL — good ground. The yields (100, 60, 30) are extraordinarily high — average ancient Palestinian wheat yields were ~7:1, exceptional yields ~15:1; Genesis 26:12 reports Isaac's hundredfold harvest as a divine blessing. The numbers signal eschatological abundance. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian 'suitable planet 4 = Earth' reading; preserve the agricultural-yield surface. Davies-Allison ICC 2.383-385.

verses.text: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
verses.translit: ho echōn ōta akouetō.
verses.notes: HEARING-FORMULA. Standard formulaic close (cf. 11:15; 13:43; Mark 4:9, 23; Rev 2:7, 11, etc.) — invites attentive interpretation. Note the absence of *akouein* (to hear) in some witnesses — Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + SBLGNT read the short form *ho echōn ōta akouetō*; Byzantine texts add *akouein* ("ears to hear"). Variant: NA28 brackets *akouein*.

verses.text: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;
verses.translit: Kai proselthontes hoi mathētai eipan autō· Dia ti en parabolais laleis autois?
verses.notes: DISCIPLES' QUESTION — opens the parable-theory excursus (vv.10-17). The question form 'why in parables' presupposes that parables OBSCURE rather than illuminate — setting up the hardening-of-hearts theme.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.
verses.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois hoti Hymin dedotai gnōnai ta mystēria tēs basileias tōn ouranōn, ekeinois de ou dedotai.
verses.notes: MYSTERIES-OF-THE-KINGDOM. *mystēria* — plural; Matthean form. Mark (4:11) and Luke (8:10) have singular *mystērion*. The pluralization suggests Matthean systematization. The insider-outsider epistemology (cf. 1QS 4:6; 4Q415-418 4QInstruction *rāz nihyeh*) parallels Qumran apocalyptic-revelation theology.

verses.text: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: hostis gar echei, dothēsetai autō kai perisseuthēsetai· hostis de ouk echei, kai ho echei arthēsetai ap' autou.
verses.notes: MATTHEAN PRINCIPLE — the cumulative-revelation rule (cf. Mt 25:29). Often called the 'Matthew effect' in sociology. Echoes Prov 1:5; Sir 3:25-26.

verses.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·
verses.translit: dia touto en parabolais autois lalō, hoti blepontes ou blepousin kai akouontes ouk akouousin oude syniousin·
verses.notes: Variant: Matthean *hoti* (because) where Markan parallel (Mk 4:12) reads *hina* (in order that) — the Matthean reading softens the predestinarian harshness of Mark. Davies-Allison ICC 2.391-393.

verses.text: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
verses.translit: kai anaplēroutai autois hē prophēteia Ēsaiou hē legousa· Akoē akousete kai ou mē synēte, kai blepontes blepsete kai ou mē idēte.
verses.notes: ISAIAH 6:9-10 CITATION (extended) — the Matthean fulfillment-formula. Matthew quotes the LXX form (close to Vaticanus); the Hebrew is more imperative ('keep hearing'); the LXX shifts to predictive future. *anaplēroutai* (is being completely fulfilled) — perfective compound.

verses.text: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: epachynthē gar hē kardia tou laou toutou, kai tois ōsin bareōs ēkousan, kai tous ophthalmous autōn ekammysan· mēpote idōsin tois ophthalmois kai tois ōsin akousōsin kai tē kardia synōsin kai epistrepsōsin, kai iasomai autous.
verses.notes: Isa 6:10 LXX cited verbatim. The verse has been the locus of major theological dispute over Israel's hardening (cf. Rom 11:7-12). **EDITOR FLAG**: do NOT translate as supersessionist 'Jews have closed their eyes' — the Isaiah-citation is an *internal* Israelite-prophet's lament, not an ethnic indictment.

verses.text: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν.
verses.translit: hymōn de makarioi hoi ophthalmoi hoti blepousin, kai ta ōta hymōn hoti akouousin.
verses.notes: Disciples' beatitude — counterpoint to the hardened-people of v.15. Cross-corpus: cf. Lk 10:23-24 (Q-parallel).

verses.text: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
verses.translit: amēn gar legō hymin hoti polloi prophētai kai dikaioi epethymēsan idein ha blepete kai ouk eidan, kai akousai ha akouete kai ouk ēkousan.
verses.notes: Eschatological-fulfillment claim — the prophets-and-righteous-ones longed for what the disciples now see. Matthean *dikaioi* (righteous ones) where Lukan parallel (Lk 10:24) reads *basileis* (kings) — possibly two different Q-versions.

verses.text: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος.
verses.translit: Hymeis oun akousate tēn parabolēn tou speirantos.
verses.notes: PARABLE-INTERPRETATION OPENS. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE** — vv.18-23 are the explicit allegorical-interpretation of the Sower parable. The canon engages this interpretation reading the 'word of the kingdom' as 'the Elohim message' and the four soil-types as planet-types. **EDITOR DO NOT pre-resolve.** Davies-Allison ICC 2.395-399; Snodgrass 2008 165-170.

verses.text: παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.
verses.translit: pantos akouontos ton logon tēs basileias kai mē synientos, erchetai ho ponēros kai harpazei to esparmenon en tē kardia autou· houtos estin ho para tēn hodon spareis.
verses.notes: FIRST-SOIL INTERPRETATION. *ho ponēros* (the evil one) — Markan parallel (Mk 4:15) reads *ho satanas*; Lukan parallel (Lk 8:12) reads *ho diabolos*. Each evangelist gives a different personification of the bird-figure of v.4. The interpretation is allegorical: *logos tēs basileias* = the kingdom-message; *kardia* = heart-soil.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν·
verses.translit: ho de epi ta petrōdē spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai euthys meta charas lambanōn auton·
verses.notes: SECOND-SOIL INTERPRETATION. Quick joyful reception, shallow root. The rocky-soil hearer.

verses.text: οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.
verses.translit: ouk echei de rhizan en heautō alla proskairos estin, genomenēs de thlipseōs ē diōgmou dia ton logon euthys skandalizetai.
verses.notes: *thlipsis ē diōgmos* (tribulation or persecution) — the Matthean community's experience locator. *skandalizetai* (stumbles/falls-away) — apostasy under pressure.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
verses.translit: ho de eis tas akanthas spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai hē merimna tou aiōnos kai hē apatē tou ploutou sympnigei ton logon, kai akarpos ginetai.
verses.notes: THIRD-SOIL INTERPRETATION. *merimna* (anxiety) — recalls Mt 6:25-34. *apatē tou ploutou* (the deceitfulness of wealth) — the second of the two thorn-chokers. Variant: some MSS add *tou bios* (of life) to the thorn-list, harmonizing with Mark/Luke.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
verses.translit: ho de epi tēn kalēn gēn spareis, houtos estin ho ton logon akouōn kai syniēis, hos dē karpophorei kai poiei ho men hekaton ho de hexēkonta ho de triakonta.
verses.notes: FOURTH-SOIL INTERPRETATION. *akouōn kai syniēis* — hearing AND understanding (Matthean keyword *synienai* — vv.13, 14, 15, 19, 51). The fourth soil is the only one that combines both. **LENS-RISK CLOSING FLAG for the Sower-parable allegorical-interpretation**: the canon's panspermia-reading must be acknowledged-without-endorsement in the Editor commentary; the surface-text is hearer-response typology.

verses.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn· Hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō speiranti kalon sperma en tō agrō autou.
verses.notes: **PARABLE OF THE TARES OPENS** (vv.24-30). **RAËLIAN CANON ENGAGES**: the canon reads the tares-parable in conjunction with the Sower as part of the seeding-of-life apparatus. Acknowledgment-without-endorsement applies. The kingdom-formula *hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn* introduces 6 of the 7 chapter-13 kingdom-parables (vv. 24, 31, 33, 44, 45, 47).

verses.text: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.
verses.translit: en de tō katheudein tous anthrōpous ēlthen autou ho echthros kai epespeiren zizania ana meson tou sitou kai apēlthen.
verses.notes: *zizania* — bearded darnel (*Lolium temulentum*), a weed-grass whose seedling is visually indistinguishable from wheat until heading; the seeds are mildly poisonous (toxic fungal symbiont). Sabotaging a neighbor's crop with darnel was a known ancient legal offense (Roman law). The realism of the parable presupposes a Galilean-agricultural audience.

verses.text: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.
verses.translit: hote de eblastēsen ho chortos kai karpon epoiēsen, tote ephanē kai ta zizania.
verses.notes: Discovery-at-heading. Until the wheat heads form ears, the two grasses look identical.

verses.text: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ; πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;
verses.translit: proselthontes de hoi douloi tou oikodespotou eipon autō· Kyrie, ouchi kalon sperma espeiras en tō sō agrō? pothen oun echei zizania?
verses.notes: The slaves' question. *oikodespotēs* (master of the house) — recurring Matthean figure (Mt 10:25; 20:1; 21:33; 24:43).

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν. οἱ δὲ δοῦλοι λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;
verses.translit: ho de ephē autois· Echthros anthrōpos touto epoiēsen. hoi de douloi legousin autō· Theleis oun apelthontes syllexōmen auta?
verses.notes: Enemy-identification. The hostile-human background recalls v.25's *echthros*.

verses.text: ὁ δέ φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·
verses.translit: ho de phēsin· Ou, mēpote syllegontes ta zizania ekrizōsēte hama autois ton siton·
verses.notes: ROOT-ENTANGLEMENT. The realistic agricultural-detail: pulling darnel mid-growth risks uprooting the wheat whose root system has intertwined. cf. Snodgrass 2008 196-198.

verses.text: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.
verses.translit: aphete synauxanesthai amphotera mechri tou therismou· kai en kairō tou therismou erō tois theristais· Syllexate prōton ta zizania kai dēsate auta eis desmas pros to katakausai auta, ton de siton synagagete eis tēn apothēkēn mou.
verses.notes: DEFERRED-SEPARATION. The eschatological-judgment harvest. Burn-darnel + barn-wheat language is standard biblical-apocalyptic eschaton imagery (cf. Joel 3:13; Rev 14:14-20).

verses.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn· Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn kokkō sinapeōs, hon labōn anthrōpos espeiren en tō agrō autou·
verses.notes: PARABLE OF THE MUSTARD SEED. *kokkos sinapeōs* — the mustard seed (*Sinapis alba* or *Brassica nigra*) was proverbially the smallest of cultivated seeds (cf. m. Nidd 5:2; m. Tehar 8:8). Mustard grew as a 2-3-meter shrub in Galilee.

verses.text: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ho mikroteron men estin pantōn tōn spermatōn, hotan de auxēthē meizon tōn lachanōn estin kai ginetai dendron, hōste elthein ta peteina tou ouranou kai kataskēnoun en tois kladois autou.
verses.notes: *ta peteina tou ouranou ... kataskēnoun en tois kladois* — direct allusion to Dan 4:12, 21 LXX (Nebuchadnezzar's great-tree dream); cf. Ezek 17:22-24; 31:6. The birds-in-branches typology = Gentile nations sheltered in Israel's kingdom-tree. The hyperbolic *dendron* (tree) for mustard-shrub matches the apocalyptic-vision register.

verses.text: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
verses.translit: Allēn parabolēn elalēsen autois· Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn zymē, hēn labousa gynē enekrypsen eis aleurou sata tria heōs hou ezymōthē holon.
verses.notes: PARABLE OF THE LEAVEN. *zymē* (leaven) is elsewhere in Jewish-biblical idiom negative (Exod 12:15-20; Mt 16:6); here used positively for kingdom-spread. *sata tria* — three measures (~22-39 liters = enough flour to feed ~100 people; cf. Gen 18:6 Abraham's hospitality to the three visitors using *tria metra*). A woman-protagonist parable (rare in the corpus).

verses.text: ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·
verses.translit: tauta panta elalēsen ho Iēsous en parabolais tois ochlois, kai chōris parabolēs ouden elalei autois·
verses.notes: PARABLE-NARRATION SUMMARY — the parabolic mode is exclusive to crowd-teaching; private disciple-teaching follows (vv.36ff).

verses.text: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς.
verses.translit: hopōs plērōthē to rhēthen dia tou prophētou legontos· Anoixō en parabolais to stoma mou, ereuxomai kekrymmena apo katabolēs.
verses.notes: FULFILLMENT-FORMULA citing Ps 78:2 (LXX 77:2). Variant: Vaticanus + Sinaiticus read *dia tou prophētou* with no name; Sinaiticus original-hand inserted *Ēsaiou* (Isaiah), an erroneous attribution since the citation is from a psalm (of Asaph); subsequent correctors removed *Ēsaiou*. NA28/SBLGNT read without prophetic-name. Davies-Allison ICC 2.426-429.

verses.text: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν. καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
verses.translit: Tote apheis tous ochlous ēlthen eis tēn oikian. kai prosēlthon autō hoi mathētai autou legontes· Diasaphēson hēmin tēn parabolēn tōn zizaniōn tou agrou.
verses.notes: PRIVATE-INTERPRETATION SETTING. *diasaphēson* (clarify, explain) — request for allegorical decoding.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
verses.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ho speirōn to kalon sperma estin ho huios tou anthrōpou·
verses.notes: TARES-ALLEGORICAL-INTERPRETATION OPENS. *huios tou anthrōpou* — son-of-man, the apocalyptic-eschatological title (cf. Dan 7:13-14). The sower-figure is now Christological.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ,
verses.translit: ho de agros estin ho kosmos· to de kalon sperma, houtoi eisin hoi huioi tēs basileias· ta de zizania eisin hoi huioi tou ponērou,
verses.notes: *ho agros = ho kosmos* (the field is the world). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the canon-reading expansion is structural here — 'the world' as cosmic-scope. The standard reading: universal-scope kingdom-mission (cf. Mt 28:19). Children-of-the-kingdom / children-of-the-evil-one — dualistic apocalyptic categories (cf. 1QS 3:13-4:26).

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.
verses.translit: ho de echthros ho speiras auta estin ho diabolos· ho de therismos synteleia aiōnos estin, hoi de theristai angeloi eisin.
verses.notes: Allegorical-key continues. *synteleia aiōnos* (end of the age) — Matthean apocalyptic phrase (recurring at 13:40, 49; 24:3; 28:20). Angels-as-reapers — cf. Joel 3:13; Rev 14:14-20.

verses.text: ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ κατακαίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος.
verses.translit: hōsper oun syllegetai ta zizania kai pyri katakaietai, houtōs estai en tē synteleia tou aiōnos.
verses.notes: Burning-darnel = eschaton-judgment image.

verses.text: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν,
verses.translit: apostelei ho huios tou anthrōpou tous angelous autou, kai syllexousin ek tēs basileias autou panta ta skandala kai tous poiountas tēn anomian,
verses.notes: *ta skandala* (the stumbling-blocks/causes-of-offense) personified. *anomian* (lawlessness) — Matthean Torah-keyword (cf. 7:23; 23:28; 24:12).

verses.text: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: kai balousin autous eis tēn kaminon tou puros· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.
verses.notes: *kaminos tou puros* (furnace of fire) — Dan 3:6 LXX echo. *klauthmos kai brygmos tōn odontōn* (weeping and gnashing of teeth) — a Matthean signature phrase (8:12; 13:42, 50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30).

verses.text: τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν. ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
verses.translit: tote hoi dikaioi eklampsousin hōs ho hēlios en tē basileia tou patros autōn. ho echōn ōta akouetō.
verses.notes: *eklampsousin hōs ho hēlios* — direct allusion to Dan 12:3 LXX (*lampousin hōs phōstēres tou ouranou*). The eschatological-resurrection-of-the-righteous tradition. Final hearing-formula closes the tares-interpretation.

verses.text: Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.
verses.translit: Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn thēsaurō kekrymmenō en tō agrō, hon heurōn anthrōpos ekrypsen, kai apo tēs charas autou hypagei kai pōlei panta hosa echei kai agorazei ton agron ekeinon.
verses.notes: HIDDEN-TREASURE PARABLE. Buried-treasure was a real Palestinian phenomenon — pre-Roman and Roman-period coin-hoards buried for safekeeping during turbulent periods. The ethical question of the finder's behavior is widely discussed in rabbinic literature (b. Bava Metzia 25b).

verses.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·
verses.translit: Palin homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō emporō zētounti kalous margaritas·
verses.notes: PEARL-OF-GREAT-PRICE PARABLE. *emporos* (wholesale merchant — long-distance trader, in distinction from *kapēlos* retail-trader). The pearl was the highest-value-by-volume commodity in the 1st-c. Mediterranean luxury trade (cf. Pliny *NH* 9.106-123).

verses.text: εὑρὼν δὲ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: heurōn de hena polytimon margaritēn apelthōn pepraken panta hosa eichen kai ēgorasen auton.
verses.notes: Total-investment commitment. Echoes v.44's *pōlei panta*.

verses.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·
verses.translit: Palin homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn sagēnē blētheisē eis tēn thalassan kai ek pantos genous synagagousē·
verses.notes: DRAGNET PARABLE. *sagēnē* — a seine net, the large Galilean fishing net dragged between two boats. *ek pantos genous* (of every kind) — Galilean lake-fish included both kosher and non-kosher species; the discrimination at sorting echoes the eschatological discrimination.

verses.text: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.
verses.translit: hēn hote eplērōthē anabibasantes epi ton aigialon kai kathisantes synelexan ta kala eis angē, ta de sapra exō ebalon.
verses.notes: Beach-sorting. *sapra* (rotten/bad) — non-kosher species (Lev 11:9-12; Deut 14:9-10 — only finned-and-scaled fish are clean).

verses.text: οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων
verses.translit: houtōs estai en tē synteleia tou aiōnos· exeleusontai hoi angeloi kai aphoriousin tous ponērous ek mesou tōn dikaiōn
verses.notes: DRAGNET-PARABLE INTERPRETATION. Angel-as-sorter echoes vv.39, 41. Eschatological discrimination of righteous / evil.

verses.text: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: kai balousin autous eis tēn kaminon tou puros· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.
verses.notes: Verbatim repetition of v.42 — formulaic close to the discrimination-parable sequence.

verses.text: Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί.
verses.translit: Synēkate tauta panta? legousin autō· Nai.
verses.notes: UNDERSTANDING-VERIFICATION. *synēkate* — the keyword *synienai* of the parable-discourse. Variant: Byzantine MSS add *Kyrie* (Lord) after *Nai*; Vaticanus + Sinaiticus omit. NA28/SBLGNT read short.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.
verses.translit: ho de eipen autois· Dia touto pas grammateus mathēteutheis tē basileia tōn ouranōn homoios estin anthrōpō oikodespotē hostis ekballei ek tou thēsaurou autou kaina kai palaia.
verses.notes: DISCIPLED-SCRIBE PARABLE. *grammateus mathēteutheis* — a passive form of *mathēteuō* (to make a disciple of, here passive 'discipled-into'). The Matthean self-portrait: Matthew is THE 'discipled scribe' bringing forth from his treasury 'new and old' — the Christian-Jewish hermeneutical method. Davies-Allison ICC 2.444-447.

verses.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tas parabolas tautas, metēren ekeithen.
verses.notes: STRUCTURAL CLOSE OF DISCOURSE 3. Matthean discourse-closing formula (cf. 7:28; 11:1; 19:1; 26:1).

verses.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;
verses.translit: kai elthōn eis tēn patrida autou edidasken autous en tē synagōgē autōn, hōste ekplēssesthai autous kai legein· Pothen toutō hē sophia hautē kai hai dynameis?
verses.notes: NAZARETH-REJECTION SCENE OPENS. *patrida* = native town (Nazareth). The crowd's question mode — surprise turning to scandal.

verses.text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός; οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;
verses.translit: ouch houtos estin ho tou tektonos huios? ouch hē mētēr autou legetai Mariam kai hoi adelphoi autou Iakōbos kai Iōsēph kai Simōn kai Ioudas?
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P103 (late 2nd / early 3rd c. CE) preserves this verse. **TEXTUAL VARIANT — KEY**: NA28/SBLGNT/Vaticanus read *ho tou tektonos huios* (the son of the carpenter); Sinaiticus reads same. Markan parallel (Mk 6:3) reads *ho tektōn, ho huios tēs Marias* (the carpenter, the son of Mary) — possibly defamatory (no father named) or possibly the original; Matthew may have softened. *tektōn* — craftsman/carpenter/builder (works in wood + stone). *adelphoi* (brothers) — the four named (James, Joseph, Simon, Judas). The Catholic/Orthodox 'perpetual virginity' tradition reads these as cousins or step-brothers (children of Joseph by a previous marriage, per *Protoevangelium Iacobi*); Protestant tradition typically reads them as full siblings.

verses.text: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν; πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα;
verses.translit: kai hai adelphai autou ouchi pasai pros hēmas eisin? pothen oun toutō tauta panta?
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P103 preserves this verse. Sisters of Jesus mentioned (anonymous, plural — at least two). *pros hēmas eisin* — 'are with us' = locally resident, married into Nazareth families.

verses.text: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eskandalizonto en autō. ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Ouk estin prophētēs atimos ei mē en tē patridi kai en tē oikia autou.
verses.notes: PAPYRUS-CROSS-COLLATED — P103 preserves this verse. PROPHET-WITHOUT-HONOR PROVERB. Widely attested both in NT (Mt 13:57; Mk 6:4; Lk 4:24; Jn 4:44; *Gos Thom* 31) and in Greco-Roman proverbial-collection literature.

verses.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai ouk epoiēsen ekei dynameis pollas dia tēn apistian autōn.
verses.notes: Matthean softening of Markan parallel (Mk 6:5 *ouk edynato* — could not). Matthew shifts from inability to election — a more theologically guarded formulation. *apistia* (lack of faith) as the inhibitor of *dynameis* (mighty works / miracles).
